q: The nausea and exhaustion is stressful! Especially trying to manage on long work days.
cx: 7 weeks, told stress is bad for the baby and stressed about it.

q: my OBGYN's nurse  stressed this to me in our introductory call so it's been in my head! Trying to keep my stress low
cx: A nurse's warning about stress in pregnancy at the first call.

q: My son woke up for a bottle this morning and I couldn’t get out of bed I was so tired. I did, thankfully, have my fiancé who did it for me, but how messed up is that? I have to be able to take care of my son.
cx: 24 weeks, more exhausted than in her first pregnancy.

q: None of this is a competition. And there is no prize for sticking to how it went in your head. Be kind to yourselves. And don't let your goals crush your spirit.
cx: A new mother after her birth and feeding went differently from plan.

q: I let it get in my head that a "natural" (vaginal) birth was what I NEEDED to do.
cx: Looking back on her birth.

q: I asked if its normal because, this is my third pregnancy, the first I had cravings but never this extreme
cx: Mid second trimester, craving extreme spice.

q: What scares me most isn’t really the pain, it’s the idea of losing control. Like not being able to communicate clearly, getting overwhelmed, or not being able to advocate for or protect myself if something feels wrong.
cx: Not pregnant; fear of birth before planning a pregnancy.

q: In the first trimester I did an at-home foot peeler mask and almost had a heart attack because I only read AFTER that it may be unsafe for baby. My feet are CRUSTY and DUSTY and an $80 pedicure isn’t something I want to pay for all the time.
cx: 19 weeks, asking what beauty treatments others were told are fine.

q: I have a prenatal massage booked for our baby moon
cx: Planning treats for a babymoon.

q: We're changing the bedding and he says, "well on the bright side we don't have to change the bedding this weekend." Bless this man because I would be losing it without him.
cx: 35 weeks, after a night of vomiting.

q: It truly is kind of cruel joke to need food and vitamins for yourself and your baby but you can't keep it down.
cx: 35 weeks.

q: I am sick of people telling me what stroller to buy, what car seat to buy, why I shouldn’t buy clothes from the baby boutique that I already bought clothes from. Why I shouldn’t have bought a crib or anything for my baby so that they can buy things for my baby.
cx: Pregnant woman tired of everyone's opinions.

q: I’ve already been shamed about the things I bought being wrong - because this other brand has great safety ratings, because I heard there was an issue with a similar product six years ago, because it’s so expensive, because I wanted to buy it for you.
cx: The reasons people give when criticising her purchases.

q: Can’t people just say congrats, and buy something off the registry and move on?
cx: Rant about advice she didn't ask for.

q: I don’t understand why when I’m sick, other women decide to tell me that they were never sick? Okay, good for you?
cx: What women say to her about sickness.

q: My husbands grandma gifted us a 3-6 month outfit yesterday, and said she didn’t get us newborn size because my husband is tall and I’m “so big”.
cx: A gift and a comment from her husband's family.

q: I’m legally single and make just under $90k/annually, so I do not qualify for Covered California’s Access Program, which would have given me immediate coverage.
cx: California, uninsured, planning prenatal care at a community clinic.

q: Could someone give me an idea or share where you went for labor/delivery & approximate costs out-of-pocket?
cx: Insurance from open enrollment starts only after her due date.

q: getting everyone to fly to middle of nowhere texas is a ridiculously expensive ask
cx: Due in December; family on both US coasts.

q: I barely even remember it now and even the hardest parts of having a newborn are easier than pregnancy was for me 😂
cx: UK, three months after her first birth, looking back on a hard pregnancy.

q: Everyone says that if the baby is fed and happy with formula or breast milk then it doesn’t matter. I just see so many posts about how great breastfeeding is that people are still breastfeeding at 2 years old and “sad” to stop. I just don’t understand and I’m starting to feel guilty for not wanting to breastfeed.
cx: 25 weeks with first, dreading breastfeeding.

q: Y’all, being pregnant with a toddler is no joke. I’m 21 weeks and just feel like this pregnancy is kicking my ass way more than my first did. That being said, my daughter has gotten a lot of screen time over the course of this pregnancy.
cx: Second pregnancy, guilty about TV time.

q: Which is so different from my first, because in my 2nd trimester I felt like a whole new human! This go around I just feel so bleh and so exhausted by things!
cx: Reply in her own thread.

q: I’m so stressed out I have to deliver a baby sick, take care of a newborn sick, have my toddler at home sick without me and god forbid if my partner gets sick.
cx: Days before a planned induction; same author as pregnant-1szchc5.

q: Postponed the induction for two days, was still a little sick but not much, ended up with a traumatizing c section
cx: Update months later.

q: We had plans for her to come visit and help us when I was late in pregnancy and then after baby came. But obviously that’s not happening
cx: 27 weeks, stay-at-home parent of a toddler; her mother, across the country, suddenly ill.

q: I don’t really have a village where I live, and the people I do have here I’m not like cry in front of or ask for real help close with.
cx: Her local support with her mother unable to come.

q: My mother in law kindly found a second hand “next to me” cot, that she got on one of her freeby sites, on Facebook, as we’re trying to stick to a budget
cx: UK, 22, expecting her second; cot turned out to be mouldy.

q: I’m just so scared if it effects me that much to just do a little stretching what the real deal will do to me 🙃
cx: 37 weeks, doing perineal massage.
